description: LockBit 2.0 is an affiliate-based Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) that has been in use since at least June 2021 as the successor to LockBit Ransomware. LockBit 2.0 has versions capable of infecting Windows and VMware ESXi virtual machines, and has been observed targeting multiple industry verticals globally.

ref-4423c257edcaf4c693d4.text:
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has a module that gathered Cloud Secrets Management Stores from password vaults within Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has the ability to leverage `sudo` for executing commands.
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR can interact with and execute Docker and Kerberos commands.
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has a module that is capable of gathering Cloud Instance Metadata to include AWS, Google Cloud Platform, and Azure.
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has the ability to identify NFS and SMB shares within the victim environment.
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has the ability to steal application tokens for CI/CD services to include Bamboo, Github, and Jenkins.
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has the ability to abuse Sudo/Cron for privilege escalation.
ref-4423c257edcaf4c693d4.title: Jay Deen. (2026, May). AI-Assisted Compromise of Mexican Water Utility with OT Implications. Retrieved September 2, 2026.

ref-51fca23de8ed76ca688a.text:
Qilin has been deployed on VMware vCenter and ESXi servers via custom PowerShell script. Qilin has also used PowerShell for discovery in vCenter and Active Directory environments.
Qilin can reboot targeted systems in safe mode to avoid detection.
Qilin has pushed a scheduled task via a Group Policy Object for payload execution.
Qilin can use AES-256 or ChaCha20 for domain-wide encryption of victim servers and workstations and RSA-4096 or RSA-2048 to secure generated encryption keys.
Qilin has pushed scheduled tasks via Group Policy Objects (GPOs) for execution. Qilin has also created a scheduled task named TVInstallRestore, configured to run at logon using the `/SC ONLOGON` argument.
ref-51fca23de8ed76ca688a.title: Thomas, W. (2024, June 12). Tracking Adversaries: The Qilin RaaS. Retrieved September 26, 2025.

ref-65970019fd9baa05199d.text:
LockBit 2.0 will not execute on hosts where the system language is set to a language spoken in the Commonwealth of Independent States region.
LockBit 2.0 can delete log files through the use of wevtutil.
LockBit 2.0 can enumerate local drive configuration.
LockBit 2.0 can enumerate system information including hostname and domain information.
LockBit 2.0 can be executed via scheduled task.
LockBit 2.0 can check if a targeted machine is using a set of Eastern European languages and exit without infection if so.
LockBit 2.0 can decode scripts and strings in loaded modules.
LockBit 2.0 can execute command line arguments in a hidden window.
LockBit 2.0 can bypass UAC through creating the Registry key `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ICM\Calibration`.
LockBit 2.0 has been observed creating accounts for persistence using simple names like "a".
LockBit 2.0 can delete itself from disk after execution.
LockBit 2.0 can disable firewall rules and anti-malware and monitoring software including Windows Defender.
LockBit 2.0 can use the PowerShell module `InvokeGPUpdate` to modify Group Policy.
LockBit 2.0 has the ability to move laterally via SMB.
LockBit 2.0 can modify Group Policy to disable Windows Defender and to automatically infect devices in Windows domains.
LockBit 2.0 can use the Windows command shell for multiple post-compromise actions on objective.
LockBit 2.0 can use standard AES and elliptic-curve cryptography algorithms to encrypt victim data.
ref-65970019fd9baa05199d.title: Elsad, A. et al. (2022, June 9). LockBit 2.0: How This RaaS Operates and How to Protect Against It. Retrieved January 24, 2025.

ref-8cd0a76849f28f67a7cd.text:
Gomir uses reverse proxy functionality that employs SSL to encrypt communications.
Gomir can start a reverse proxy to initiate connections to arbitrary endpoints in victim networks.
Gomir probes arbitrary network endpoints for TCP connectivity.
Gomir uses a custom encryption algorithm for content sent to command and control infrastructure.
Gomir will configure a crontab for process execution to start the backdoor on reboot if it is not initially running under group 0 privileges.
Gomir collects information about directory and file structures, including total number of subdirectories, total number of files, and total size of files on infected systems.
Gomir creates a systemd service named `syslogd` for persistence.
GoBear is installed through droppers masquerading as legitimate, signed software installers.
Gomir checks the effective group ID of its process when initially executed to determine if it is in group 0, denoting superuser privileges in Linux environments.
Gomir reads command line arguments and parses them for functionality when executed from a Linux shell, and can execute arbitrary strings passed to it as shell commands.
Gomir deletes its original executable and terminates its original process after creating a systemd service.
Gomir collects information on infected systems such as hostname, username, CPU, and RAM information.
Gomir periodically communicates to its command and control infrastructure through HTTP POST requests.
Gomir uses Base64-encoded content in HTTP communications to command and control infrastructure.
Gomir collects network information on infected systems such as listing interface names, MAC and IP addresses, and IPv6 addresses.
ref-8cd0a76849f28f67a7cd.title: Symantec Threat Hunter Team. (2024, May 16). Springtail: New Linux Backdoor Added to Toolkit. Retrieved January 17, 2025.

ref-bced9f30c80f5898db48.text:
Exbyte decodes and decrypts data stored in the configuration file with a key provided on the command line during execution.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware modifies the victim Registry to allow for elevated execution.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware can timestomp files for defense evasion and anti-forensics purposes.
Exbyte checks for the presence of a configuration file before completing execution.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware injects into a newly-created `svchost.exe` process prior to device encryption.
Exbyte will self-delete if a hard-coded configuration file is not found.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware executes as a service when deployed.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware modifies volume shadow copies during execution in a way that destroys them on the victim machine.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware exploits a vulnerability in the RTCore64.sys driver (CVE-2019-16098) to enable privilege escalation and defense evasion when run as a service.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware can terminate running services.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware modifies the Windows firewall during execution.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware can identify network shares connected to the victim machine.
Exbyte checks whether the process is running with privileged local access during execution.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware deletes itself following device encryption.
Exbyte calls `ShellExecuteW` with the `IpOperation` parameter `RunAs` to launch `explorer.exe` with elevated privileges.
BlackByte 2.0 Ransomware is a ransomware variant associated with BlackByte operations.
Exbyte exfiltrates collected data to online file hosting sites such as `Mega.co.nz`.
ref-bced9f30c80f5898db48.title: Microsoft Incident Response. (2023, July 6). The five-day job: A BlackByte ransomware intrusion case study. Retrieved December 16, 2024.

LockBit 3.0 has the ability to discover external storage devices.

LockBit 3.0 can delete itself from disk.

LockBit 3.0 can change the Registry values for Group Policy refresh time, to disable SmartScreen, and to disable Windows Defender.

LockBit 3.0 can encrypt targeted data using the AES-256, ChaCha20, or RSA-2048 algorithms.
LockBit 3.0 can enumerate local drive configuration.
LockBit 3.0 can identify network shares on compromised systems.
LockBit 3.0 can make execution dependent on specific parameters including a unique passphrase and the system language of the targeted host not being found on a set exclusion list.
LockBit 3.0 can create and check for a mutex containing a hash of the `MachineGUID` value at execution to prevent running more than one instance.
LockBit 3.0 can enumerate system hostname and domain.
LockBit 3.0 can enable options for propogation through Group Policy Objects.
LockBit 3.0 can bypass UAC to execute code with elevated privileges through an elevated Component Object Model (COM) interface.
LockBit 3.0 can encrypt C2 communications with AES.
LockBit 3.0 can terminate targeted processes and services related to security, backup, database management, and other applications that could stop or interfere with encryption.
LockBit 3.0 can Base64-encode C2 communication.
LockBit 3.0 can enable automatic logon through the `SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon` Registry key.
LockBit 3.0 can reboot the infected host into Safe Mode.
LockBit 3.0 can use SMB for lateral movement.
The LockBit 3.0 payload is decrypted at runtime.
LockBit 3.0 can exclude files associated with core system functions from encryption.
The LockBit 3.0 payload includes an encrypted main component.
LockBit 3.0 will not affect machines with language settings matching a defined exlusion list of mainly Eastern European languages.
LockBit 3.0 can delete volume shadow copies.
LockBit 3.0 can use HTTP to send victim host information to C2.
